title: Simulation Task
description: Develop a multi-agent simulation system that models the spread of mask-wearing behavior through social networks.
simulation_focus: Predict agents' mask-wearing behavior over day 30 - day 39 (last ten days) based on their attributes, social connections, and past behavior
Model information propagation and behavioral changes triggered by social influence and government intervention starting on Day 10

data_files.agent_attributes.csv: Contains demographic and behavioral attributes of each agent, including age, occupation, risk perception, and social connection counts
data_files.social_network.json: Contains structured data representing a social network. Each entry corresponds to a user (identified by a unique integer ID), and the values describe the different types of relationships that user has with others. Data Structure: The top-level structure is a dictionary ({} in JSON). Keys: Each key is a unique user ID (as an integer, e.g., 0, 1, 2, etc.). Values: Each value is another dictionary with the following fields: "family": a list of user IDs representing family connections. "work_school": a list of user IDs representing colleagues or schoolmates. "community": a list of user IDs representing community-level acquaintances. "all": a merged list of all user IDs connected to the user across the three categories above.
data_files.train_data.csv: Time series data for the first 30 days, used for training the model

RMSE.description: Root Mean Square Error measuring overall predictive accuracy of mask adoption rates
RMSE.interpretation: Directly interpretable as percentage deviations due to the 0-1 range

Peak Adoption Rate Error.description: Measures model accuracy in predicting maximum mask adoption during intervention

Time-to-Peak Error.description: Measures model accuracy in predicting the time lag from intervention to peak behavior change

key_patterns.name: Multiplex degree heterogeneity
key_patterns.description: Agents have different intended/observed numbers of ties across family, work/school, and community layers; family degrees are typically small/tight, work/school moderate, and community broader and more skewed.
key_patterns.relevance: Determines contact opportunities and influence exposure by layer; supports layer-specific influence weights and contact rates.

key_patterns.name: Partial reciprocity of ties
key_patterns.description: Edges in social_network.json may be directed; not all ties are reciprocated.
key_patterns.relevance: Influence may be asymmetric; calibration should decide to use directed influence or symmetrize per layer.

key_patterns.name: High clustering in family layer
key_patterns.description: Family ties likely form closed triads; work/school moderate clustering; community lowest clustering.
key_patterns.relevance: Clustering affects cascade dynamics and redundancy of information; informs configuration or rewiring targets if generating networks.

key_patterns.name: Assortativity by age and occupation
key_patterns.description: Family ties are assortative by age_group; work/school ties assort by occupation (e.g., Students linked to Students).
key_patterns.relevance: Assortativity shapes diffusion boundaries; match assortativity coefficients when generating or pruning networks.

key_patterns.name: Risk perception correlates with initial mask wearing
key_patterns.description: Higher risk_perception is associated with initial_mask_wearing = 1.
key_patterns.relevance: Set baseline adoption propensities or priors by risk_perception; include as covariate in adoption probability.

key_patterns.name: State inertia (persistence)
key_patterns.description: Agents tend to remain in their current state across days (wearing → wearing; not wearing → not wearing).
key_patterns.relevance: Include habit/persistence terms in transition model to avoid overreactive dynamics.

key_patterns.name: Information exposure increases next-day adoption
key_patterns.description: received_info at day t-1 increases P(wearing_mask at t), with possible diminishing effects beyond 1–3 days.
key_patterns.relevance: Calibrate info efficacy and decay; model an info memory state.

key_patterns.name: Peer influence via neighbor prevalence
key_patterns.description: The fraction of neighbors wearing masks (overall or by layer) is positively associated with adoption; family influence strongest.
key_patterns.relevance: Supports a layer-weighted peer influence model (linear threshold or logistic with neighbor fraction).

key_patterns.name: Layer overlap of ties
key_patterns.description: Some dyads appear in multiple layers (e.g., family members who also work together), increasing tie strength.
key_patterns.relevance: Use overlap (multiplexity) to upweight influence on those edges.

key_patterns.name: Potential mismatch between intended and realized degrees
key_patterns.description: total_connections in agent_attributes may not perfectly match degrees observed in social_network.json.
key_patterns.relevance: Use as a data quality check; if generating/sampling edges, target the intended degree sequence.

key_distributions.name: Risk perception
key_distributions.parameters: Fit Beta(α, β) to risk_perception from agent_attributes.csv.

key_distributions.name: Initial mask-wearing prevalence
key_distributions.description: Share of agents with initial_mask_wearing = 1 (or day 0 wearing_mask in train_data).
key_distributions.parameters: Bernoulli(p0) with p0 = mean(initial_mask_wearing) or mean(wearing_mask | day=0).

key_distributions.name: Layer-specific degree distributions
key_distributions.description: Degrees by family, work_school, community per agent.
key_distributions.parameters: Fit Negative Binomial or Poisson for each layer; report mean and dispersion (r, p) per layer from social_network.json or agent_attributes.csv.

key_distributions.name: Aggregate degree distribution
key_distributions.parameters: Fit Negative Binomial; parameters from agent_attributes.csv.

key_distributions.name: Markov transition probabilities
key_distributions.parameters: p01 = P(0→1), p10 = P(1→0), p00, p11 computed from train_data.csv; estimate separately with and without received_info(t-1).

key_distributions.name: Information exposure rate
key_distributions.description: Probability an agent receives info on a day.
key_distributions.parameters: p_info = mean(received_info) per day and overall; optionally fit over time or by layer degree.

key_distributions.name: Reciprocity by layer
key_distributions.description: Fraction of edges that are mutual.
key_distributions.parameters: recip_layer = 2 * |mutual edges| / |directed edges| computed per layer from social_network.json.

key_distributions.name: Clustering by layer
key_distributions.parameters: Average clustering coefficient C_family > C_work > C_community; compute via undirected projection.

key_distributions.name: Assortativity coefficients
key_distributions.parameters: r_age and r_occ per layer via Newman assortativity from social_network.json plus agent_attributes.csv.

key_relationships.relationship: Positive association; higher risk_perception predicts initial adoption.
key_relationships.strength: Estimate via logistic regression; expect medium to strong.

key_relationships.relationship: Positive causal effect (lag-1): info exposure increases next-day adoption and reduces abandonment.
key_relationships.strength: Estimate via difference in conditional probabilities or logistic regression; typically medium.

key_relationships.relationship: Positive peer influence; family strongest weight, then work/school, then community.
key_relationships.strength: Estimate via logistic regression with layer-specific fractions; expect strong in family, moderate elsewhere.

key_relationships.relationship: Demographics predict layer degrees (students high school/work degree; retirees low work, higher family/community).
key_relationships.strength: Estimate via GLM for count data; moderate.

key_relationships.relationship: Interaction: risk_perception moderates susceptibility to peer prevalence.
key_relationships.strength: Estimate interaction term; small to moderate.

key_relationships.relationship: Agents with more incoming ties receive info more often.

layer_weights.source: Recommended default based on social context strength; refine with social_network.json + train_data.csv peer effect estimation
layer_weights.notes: Rescale such that max(layer_weights)=1. Calibrate by matching adoption elasticity to neighbor wearing by layer.

reciprocity_rate_layer.value: Compute per layer: reciprocity = 2*|mutual edges|/|directed edges|
reciprocity_rate_layer.notes: If using undirected influence, report for QA but not used directly.

clustering_coefficients.value: Compute average local clustering per layer after symmetrization
clustering_coefficients.notes: Use to validate/generate network; clustering drives reinforcement.

assortativity_age.value: Compute Newman assortativity r by age_group, per layer
assortativity_age.notes: Target when synthesizing networks from degree sequences.

assortativity_occupation.value: Compute Newman assortativity r by occupation, per layer

degree_distribution_params.notes: Use empirical if available; else intended degrees. Validate goodness-of-fit vs Poisson.

overlap_multiplexity.value: Mean Jaccard overlap of neighbor sets across layers
overlap_multiplexity.notes: Use as weight multiplier for edges appearing in multiple layers (e.g., ×1.2).

symmetrize_edges.source: Modeling choice informed by behavioral reciprocity
symmetrize_edges.notes: If influence should be mutual; else keep directed and use in-degree for exposure.

initial_prevalence_p0.notes: Use train_data day 0 if available to override CSV boolean.

p_adopt_baseline.source: train_data.csv (+ derived neighbor features from social_network.json)
p_adopt_baseline.notes: Intercept of logistic model for adoption when no info and no peers wearing.

beta_peer_family.notes: Expect largest magnitude; translates to influence weight.

beta_peer_work_school.notes: Moderate effect; calibrate jointly with layer_weights.

beta_peer_community.notes: Smallest effect; may be near zero.

beta_risk_perception.value: Logistic coefficient on risk_perception for adoption
beta_risk_perception.notes: Apply to both adoption and reduced abandonment (with opposite sign).

beta_risk_peer_interaction.value: Interaction term between risk_perception and neighbor_wearing_fraction
beta_risk_peer_interaction.notes: Captures differential susceptibility; include if significant.

habit_persistence_gamma.value: Log-odds coefficient for wearing_mask(t-1) in logistic model
habit_persistence_gamma.notes: Controls state inertia; typically large positive.

decision_rule.value: Layer-weighted logistic adoption with stochastic updates
decision_rule.notes: Alternative: linear threshold with heterogeneity; choose based on fit.

threshold_distribution.value: If using threshold model, fit Beta(α_thr, β_thr) to implied thresholds matching adoption elasticity
threshold_distribution.source: Derived from logistic fit via mapping or ABC
threshold_distribution.notes: Only if logistic underfits tipping behavior.

p_info_external.value: Mean(received_info) not explained by peer messages; estimate residual after peer-generated info model

p_info_from_neighbor.value: Per wearing neighbor per day probability of sending info (q_layer), fit per layer
p_info_from_neighbor.notes: Fit a message-passing model: P(received_info) ≈ 1 - Π(1 - q_layer) over wearing neighbors.

info_memory_decay_half_life_days.source: Recommended default; refine via lagged effect decay in train_data.csv
info_memory_decay_half_life_days.notes: Implement as exponential decay of info influence with half-life ~3 days.

campaign_targeting_policy.value: Optional: target high-betweenness or low-adoption clusters
campaign_targeting_policy.notes: Used for intervention scenarios; not needed for baseline calibration.

time_step_days.notes: Each simulation tick equals one day.

contacts_per_day_by_layer.source: Recommended default; refine using adoption responsiveness by layer
contacts_per_day_by_layer.notes: If modeling sampled contacts rather than full-neighborhood influence.

update_scheme.value: Synchronous daily updates using t-1 states

preprocessing_steps.step: Parse and validate IDs and booleans
preprocessing_steps.purpose: Ensure agent_id alignment across files; convert wearing_mask and received_info to {0,1}.
Verify total_connections equals sum of layer degrees in agent_attributes.csv; flag or fix inconsistencies.
Construct family, work_school, community graphs; deduplicate edges; decide on symmetrization.
Degrees, reciprocity, clustering, assortativity, multiplex overlap for parameterization and validation.
From social_network.json and train_data.csv, compute neighbor_wearing_fraction per layer at t-1 for each agent-day.
Compute received_info(t-1), and optionally decayed info memory for modeling carryover.
Forward-fill states or drop gaps; ensure consecutive daily transitions per agent.
Split by time (e.g., first 70% days train, last 30% validate) to prevent leakage.

calibration_strategy.calibration_approach: Two-stage, then simulation-based refinement. Stage 1: Fit an agent-day logistic regression (or mixed-effects) for wearing_mask(t) with covariates: wearing_mask(t-1), received_info(t-1) (and its decayed memory), neighbor_wearing_fraction by layer (t-1), risk_perception, age_group, occupation, and key interactions (risk × peers). Extract baseline adoption/abandonment, info efficacy, and layer-specific peer coefficients. Stage 2: Calibrate network-related parameters (layer_weights, contact sampling, multiplex edge weights) to align the simulated effects with the estimated regression coefficients by mapping logistic coefficients to simulation influence weights. Stage 3: Run the ABM and use simulation-based inference (grid search or Bayesian optimization/ABC) to minimize discrepancy between simulated and empirical targets: daily prevalence, adoption/abandonment rates, and response to info. Iterate until convergence.
calibration_strategy.validation_strategy: Out-of-sample time backtesting on the held-out period. Validate: (1) Prevalence curve: RMSE/MAE between simulated and observed wearing rates over time. (2) Transition rates: Compare P(0→1) and P(1→0) overall and conditional on received_info across time; use calibration plots. (3) Peer effect: In simulation logs, regress adoption on neighbor_wearing_fraction and compare coefficients to Stage 1 estimates. (4) Network diagnostics: Ensure simulated network (if generated) matches degree distributions, clustering, and assortativity. (5) Subgroup fit: Compare prevalence and adoption rates by age_group and occupation. (6) Sensitivity analysis: Vary key parameters ±10–20% and assess stability.

file_summaries:
Semantic metadata summary for agent_attributes.csv

- Overall structure and type
  - CSV, flat table; one row per agent (individual).
  - Columns include integers, floats, booleans, and categorical strings.
  - agent_id is the unique primary key.

- Meaning of columns
  - agent_id (int): Unique identifier for an agent.
  - age (int): Agent’s age in years.
  - age_group (categorical): Age band label (e.g., Youth, Young Adult, Middle Age), derived from age.
  - occupation (categorical): Socioeconomic/role category (e.g., Student, Blue Collar, White Collar); informs work/school layer membership.
  - risk_perception (float 0–1): Agent-specific propensity to perceive/act on risk; higher likely means greater baseline probability to wear masks and/or respond to peers.
  - initial_mask_wearing (bool): Agent’s initial adoption state at t0.
  - family_connections (int): Intended number of ties in the family/household layer.
  - work_school_connections (int): Intended number of ties in the work or school layer.
  - community_connections (int): Intended number of ties in broader community/social layer.
  - total_connections (int): Sum of the three layer-specific degrees; equals family + work_school + community.

- Relationships or nested elements
  - No nested structures or explicit edges; this file specifies per-agent degree targets by layer, not who the connections are with.
  - total_connections is a derived consistency check and should equal the sum of layer degrees.
  - No household IDs, workplace IDs, or community group IDs are provided; these must be synthesized.

- How this data should inform simulation entities/interactions
  - Entities: Initialize one Agent per row with attributes: demographic (age, age_group, occupation), behavioral state (initial_mask_wearing), and psychology (risk_perception).
  - Network topology: Use family/work_school/community connection counts as degree sequences to generate a multiplex network (one layer per context). Construct edges stochastically (e.g., configuration model) or with constraints (e.g., assortativity by age/occupation, clustering for families).
  - Interaction rules: Peer influence on mask adoption should operate over the multiplex; optionally weight layers differently (e.g., family > work/school > community).
  - Decision model inputs: risk_perception modulates susceptibility to social influence and/or baseline adoption; age_group and occupation can parameterize contact patterns and influence weights; initial_mask_wearing sets t0 state.
  - Data caveats: Occupation/age inconsistencies may exist (e.g., very young with non-student occupations); consider validation or correction before network generation and behavior modeling.

Semantic metadata summary for social_network.json

- Overall data structure and type:
  - JSON object (dictionary) mapping agent IDs (as strings) to a nested object.
  - Each agent’s object contains arrays of integers representing other agent IDs.

- Meaning of keys/columns:
  - family: adjacency list of close-kin ties for the agent.
  - work_school: adjacency list of work or school ties.
  - community: adjacency list of broader community ties.
  - all: union of family, work_school, and community for convenience (deduplicated).

- Relationships and nested elements:
  - Multi-layer (multiplex) social network: three context-specific layers plus an aggregated view.
  - Entries are adjacency lists; edges may be directed (reciprocity is not guaranteed in the file).
  - No weights or timestamps are provided; only categorical tie types.
  - Agent IDs are integers referenced as list elements; top-level keys are stringified IDs.

- How this data should inform simulation entities or interactions:
  - Agents: one agent per top-level key; maintain agent state (e.g., mask-wearing boolean/probability).
  - Network construction:
    - Build separate graphs per layer (family, work_school, community); optionally add an aggregate graph from all.
    - Consider symmetrizing edges if the behavioral influence should be mutual; otherwise keep directed for asymmetric influence.
    - Store edge attribute layer to differentiate tie contexts.
  - Interaction modeling:
    - Use layer-specific contact rates and influence strengths (e.g., family > work_school > community).
    - At each timestep, sample contacts per layer or use all neighbors; compute adoption/abandonment via a chosen diffusion rule (e.g., independent cascade, linear threshold with layer weights).
    - The all list is a convenience for aggregate influence; for context-aware dynamics, use the three specific lists instead.
  - Preprocessing checks:
    - Validate that all IDs referenced exist as agents.
    - Deduplicate neighbor lists (all should already be a union).
    - Decide on handling of non-reciprocal ties and potential self-loops (none observed in sample).

Semantic metadata summary for train_data.csv

- Data type and structure
  - CSV; flat, rectangular panel (time-series by agent).
  - One row = one observation for a specific agent on a specific day.
  - Composite primary key: (agent_id, day).

- Columns and meanings
  - day (int): Discrete simulation timestep (e.g., t = 0, 1, 2, ...).
  - agent_id (int): Unique identifier for an agent.
  - wearing_mask (bool): Agent’s behavioral state at that day (1 = wearing, 0 = not).
  - received_info (bool): Whether the agent received mask-related information on that day (e.g., message/exposure), irrespective of whether they adopted.

- Relationships and temporal structure
  - Rows are ordered by time within each agent; forms a longitudinal sequence.
  - Transitions can be derived between consecutive days for each agent:
    - Adoption: wearing_mask(t-1)=0 → wearing_mask(t)=1
    - Abandonment: 1 → 0
    - Persistence: 0 → 0 or 1 → 1
  - received_info is a contemporaneous exogenous signal; its effect is typically modeled on next-step behavior (lagged influence).

- How to use this data in the simulation
  - Initialization
    - Set initial wearing_mask state for each agent at day 0 (or first available day).
    - Optionally initialize an “info memory” state if modeling carryover effects.
  - Parameter learning/calibration
    - Estimate baseline transition probabilities without info:
      - P(adopt | no-info), P(abandon | no-info), persistence rates.
    - Estimate info efficacy (uplift):
      - Δ P(adopt | received_info), and any change in abandonment.
    - Fit agent-level or population-level heterogeneity (e.g., random effects by agent_id).
    - If modeling lag/decay, estimate effect of received_info at t-1 (and possibly longer lags) on wearing_mask at t.
  - Simulation mechanics
    - Agents have at least two states: behavior (wearing_mask) and info_exposure (received_info or its memory).
    - Social network is not present in this file; must be generated or supplied separately.
      - Use this file to calibrate individual propensities; use the network to generate endogenous received_info events (peer messages) during simulation.
    - External campaigns/broadcasts can set received_info for targeted agents/days based on observed patterns.
  - Validation
    - Compare simulated time-series (adoption/abandonment rates and prevalence) with empirical rates computed from the CSV.

Notes/assumptions
- Booleans may need parsing from string to boolean.
- Missing days per agent, if any, require interpolation or careful transition estimation.
- No contact/edge data or demographics provided; limits direct estimation of peer effects—use this data for individual transition dynamics and info-response, not for network structure.
